meta.title: Fogar
meta.description: An AI ecosystem for your home: voice, a gateway that connects your clients and your smart home, and open source code.

d.portada: A compatible screen or speaker can be a client.
d.gateway: It brings together voice, clients, home automation and OpenClaw.
d.gateway2: Clients only talk to the gateway: it decides who gets in and with which agent.
d.voz: The one you choose. It's detected on the device itself. It's just another client.
d.vozEjemplo: e.g. “What do I have on this week?”
baldaH2: Fogar doesn't bring its own suite.
d.lampara: Fogar turns on the lamp through Home Assistant.
d.radio: A speaker hooked up to a light client: an ESP32 is enough.
d.libreta: Your second brain, where you already write.
d.nota: Fogar TV and the voice client (macOS, Android and Linux) already work. The web panel will be the main interface.
d.recorrido: A walk through a living room: a stone fireplace with a fire and a TV above it, a speaker, an oak shelf with a lamp, a radio, a clock and a notebook, and a plain wall.
d.teleSr: The TV shows Fogar TV: the time, the date, a timer and what's playing. A line of light writes “Fogar” and follows the walk.

instala.lead: One step, on a machine of your own:
instala.requisitos: It needs Linux with user systemd and OpenClaw 2026.6.11 or later, on the same machine or over an SSH tunnel.

usas.lead: Fogar sits on top of what you already have at home and takes it to your compatible screens and speakers.
filas: Fogar talks to it over MCP and asks it for things around the house. It works the other way too: Home Assistant's voice assistant can be Fogar.
It orchestrates, with its memory, its agents and its scheduled tasks, and calls Home Assistant, Obsidian, Notion… over MCP.
Whichever one you already have set up in OpenClaw.
whisper.cpp and Kokoro on your network. Or ElevenLabs: if it transcribes, it gets your audio; if it speaks, it gets the text of the answers.
usas.protocolo: Everything goes through fogar-gateway. If you want to write your own client, the protocol is documented.

casa.titulo: What leaves home and what doesn't
casa.cuerpo: Your voice doesn't go through a Fogar cloud service, but something always leaves: what you ask the AI model reaches whoever serves it. If you use ElevenLabs, or a tunnel to talk to it from outside, your audio or your answers go through them too. You choose every piece: your data goes where you decide and doesn't end up scattered around.
